primary_meaning: Intimate, permanent divine care, remembrance, and protection (God holding or engraving His people on the palms of His hands)
primary_basis: Isaiah 40:11–12 (gathering lambs in arms / measuring waters in the hollow of the hand, linked in teaching on God’s tender yet sovereign hold)
John 10:28–29 and related NT pastoral imagery of none snatching from the Father’s hand (read back onto kaph passages)

alternatives.meaning: Divine power, creative measurement, and sovereign control over creation
basis: Isaiah 40:12 (waters measured in the hollow/kaph of the hand)
Psalm 95:4–5 and similar creation texts emphasizing the hand’s grasp

alternatives.meaning: Human agency, labor, giving/receiving, or violence (the palm as the active surface of the hand)
basis: General OT usage of kaph for clapping, striking, holding tools or weapons, or open-handed gesture (e.g., Proverbs, Psalms, Job)
Ritual or worship contexts of lifted or open palms

alternatives.meaning: Christ’s crucified wounds / marks of sacrifice remembered in the palms
basis: Typological reading of Isaiah 49:16 together with crucifixion nail-marks (John 20:25–27; Luke 24:39–40)
Devotional and hymnic tradition linking the two

alternatives.meaning: No distinct fixed symbol; simply the anatomical palm/hollow with ordinary literal or idiomatic force
basis: Lexicons and many historical-critical commentaries treating kaph primarily as body-part vocabulary rather than a standing emblem

notes: In published Christian preaching, devotion, and biblical theology the Isaiah 49:16 image overwhelmingly supplies the dominant symbolic reading of kaph when the term is treated as a symbol rather than a mere body part. Other senses appear regularly but are usually contextual or secondary. No major competing ‘official’ symbol displaces the care/remembrance motif in mainstream teaching.
